finding: At 9 p.m., half of Chicago's residents need more than 10 minutes to get moving: a step-free roll to a bus or an accessible train, and the wait for it. On the Far Southwest Side, 33% need more than 15; on the North Side, 1%.

ledger.source: CTA GTFS schedule; OpenStreetMap walk network; 2020 Census blocks
ledger.units: 13,231 blocks of ⅛ mile on Chicago’s address grid; 2,746,388 residents (2020 Census)
method: Weekday Tuesday 10 November 2026, departures 20:30–21:30; every CTA bus route, and trains at accessible stations only

Step-free walk (no stairs) on OpenStreetMap (1 Nov 2026) from each block’s centre, by any walkway within 100 m, to each route’s nearest stop within four blocks (½ mile), at 3 ft/s (MUTCD 2009, 4E.06: the speed for timing a whole crossing; 3.5 ft/s for clearance)
Minutes until moving = that walk + half the time between buses or trains at the stop; each block prints the least
Printed as a line-printer map after SYMAP (1963–66): one character per block, tone by overprinting
caveats: Scheduled service, not real arrivals; one direction at the nearest stop; a rider arriving at random
CTA: all buses and railcars accessible; bus stops themselves (curb, shelter, snow) are not checked
Blocks with no walkway within 100 m print blank; residents placed by their 2020 block’s internal point
